newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INP cancels funding meant for NZ W&H stake.
newsitem.headline: INP cancels funding meant for NZ W&H stake.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Plc's (INP) finance director James Parkinson said a funding facility earmarked for the purchase of the 15 percent of Wilson & Horton shares the media group does not already own had been cancelled.

"We raised a 400 million (Irish) pound bank facility in Ireland to make the bid, of which part was to buy the full part of Wilson & Horton," Parkinson told Reuters after Wilson & Horton's annual meeting on Thursday.
"At this stage we have quite a lot of it unspent because we have only been successful in getting 85 percent of Wilson & Horton.

"There has been little point at this stage in continuing to pay fees on the part of the facility which was earmarked for the 15 percent, so we have cancelled it to stop the facility fees continuing to run on (it)," he added.
He said the firm cancelled 130 million pounds of the original 400 million pound facility.
He declined comment on whether INP would seek to raise funds in the future to seek to buy the remaining 15 percent in W&H.
INP is controlled by Tony O'Reilly.
